title: What does a tire company know about food?
summary: Josh and Chuck explore the Michelin Guide, the restaurant rating guide published by the tire company Michelin. They cover the company's origins with Andre and Edouard Michelin in the 1889 era, the Michelin Man (Bibendum) mascot, and why the guide was created in 1900 to encourage road trips and tire sales. They explain the star system (introduced 1931), the five criteria for stars, the Bib Gourmand and "plate" symbols, Green Star, covers, and regional specialty symbols. They describe the anonymous inspectors and their training, criticism of the guide (including chef Bernard Loiseau's suicide, the "cheddar gate" lawsuit by Marc Veyrat, and chefs who gave back stars such as Sébastien Bras and Jiro Ono's sushi restaurant), the guide's expansion to America and Asia, and close with listener mail from Kyle in Phoenix.

entities.name: The Inspector Sits Down at the Table

segments.title: Intro and Michelin tire connection
segments.summary: Hosts open with banter about Michelin-starred restaurants, then introduce the fact that the Michelin Guide is published by a tire company, and begin the history of Michelin brothers and early tire making.

segments.title: Michelin Man and origins of the guide
segments.summary: The Michelin Man, originally named Bibendum, debuted in 1898 with a poster. The guide began in 1900 to encourage road trips and increase tire sales. Early history includes free distribution, restaurant recommendations from 1906, and the star system introduced in 1931.

segments.title: Expansion abroad and first American guide
segments.summary: The first guide outside France appeared in Belgium in 1904. The first American guide covered New York City in 2005 and drew criticism for focusing on French restaurants. The modern guide covers more than 40 restaurants in 34 countries and the US cities of New York, California, Chicago and Washington, D.C.

segments.title: Star criteria and star counts
segments.summary: The hosts explain the five criteria for stars, which focus only on food: ingredient quality, flavor and technique mastery, chef personality, harmony of flavors, and consistency across visits. They note how three stars signal consistently perfect food and give worldwide star counts.

segments.title: Bib Gourmand, plate symbol, Green Star, covers and regional symbols
segments.summary: The hosts explain the Bib Gourmand (good value meals, around forty dollars per person), the plate symbol for simply good food, the Green Star for sustainability, covers for ambiance, and regional symbols such as tapas toothpicks, beer mugs, grapes and sake bottles.

segments.title: Anonymous inspectors
segments.summary: The hosts describe Michelin inspectors as trained, experienced hospitality professionals who go through about a year of vetting and apprenticeship, eat alone and anonymously, and visit many restaurants a year. They discuss the difficulty of staying anonymous and the loneliness of the job.

segments.title: Criticism and controversies
segments.summary: The hosts cover criticism of the guide: the 2003 suicide of chef Bernard Loiseau after fears of losing stars, Daniel Boulud's relaxed reaction to losing a star, Gordon Ramsay's reaction, Sébastien Bras returning his stars, the cheddar gate lawsuit by Marc Veyrat, and the removal of Jiro's sushi stars because the restaurant is too hard to book.

segments.title: Guide's evolution and Asian expansion
segments.summary: The guide became less Franco-centric in the twenty-first century. Paris and Tokyo have the most starred restaurants. Singapore hawker stall and a Taipei street stall are mentioned as honored, and the hosts discuss the frustration of waiting in lines for food.

segments.title: Listener mail from Kyle in Phoenix
segments.summary: Kyle says he finished listening to the entire back catalog, praises episodes and the Teddy the beaver story, and says Josh's bat comment in an earlier episode seemed to predict COVID-19. Hosts respond briefly about the origin of the virus.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts thank listeners and give the email address and iHeartRadio app information.
